codeReview.summary: The alias-routing change in `hmmer.py` is scoped correctly: `rhesus` now resolves to `macaque` for custom/local HMM lookup while the legacy ANARCI fallback remains available. I found no blocking runtime defects in the diff, but two new assertions are weaker than the feature contract they are meant to prove.

issues.description: `test_rhesus_and_macaque_produce_identical_output()` only compares `scheme`, `chain_type`, `v_gene`, and `j_gene`, so numbering columns can still drift without failing the test. The feature contract called for proving rhesus and macaque produce identical renumbering output.

`test_macaque_renumbering_unchanged_regression()` guards its core check with `if "30" in result.columns`, so it silently passes if Kabat position `30` disappears from the output. Assert that the column exists before checking the residue to make the regression meaningful.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The shared architecture doc does not match the live HMM fallback logic: it says the order is LocalHMMBuilder -> Legacy ANARCI -> G3, but `hmmer.py` goes to G3 whenever the species/chain is usable there and only uses Numbering when G3 lacks support or is forced.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/library/architecture.md:30-34 documents Legacy before G3, while src/sadie/renumbering/aligners/hmmer.py:159-166 branches to Numbering only when `single_species`/`chain` are unavailable in G3, and src/sadie/renumbering/clients/g3.py:23-29,45-48 defines which species are excluded from G3.

summary: Pass. The core `rhesus` -> `macaque` routing fix in `hmmer.py` looks correct and backward-compatible, with only non-blocking test-strength gaps noted in the new species-contract assertions.
